newsitem.title: USA: Oil services stocks soften as supply increases.
newsitem.headline: Oil services stocks soften as supply increases.

text.p: Shares of oil and gas services companies softened Thursday after data on U.S. natural gas storage levels showed total supply about 16 percent over last year, analysts said.

Rowan Cos Inc dropped 1-7/8 to 18-7/8, Noble Drilling Corp fell 7/8 to 16-3/4 and Global Marine Inc shed one to 17-7/8. Diamond Offshore Drilling Inc lost 3-5/8 to 57-3/8 and Falcon Drilling Co Inc also softened.
"There's some nervousness. The stocks are reacting to seeing the storage data being higher than last year," said Morgan Keegan & Co analyst William Neal McAtee.
U.S. natural gas storage levels are up about 16 percent over last year, with eastern region stocks running 56 percent over 1996.
McAtee said that last year's levels were at record lows, which distorts comparisons.

"The warm weather has really pulled prices way back. With the weather so warm, no one is drawing down supply. Supply levels are almost 20 percent higher than last year," said Moultrie Dotterer, an analyst Scott & Stringfellow.
The moderate U.S. weather outlook may continue to pressure oil and gas prices over the near-term, which will weigh heavily on oil services stocks, analysts said.
But some analysts said the recent stock stock weakness was an overreaction. On a long-term basis, oil services companies will likely outperform the market, analysts said.
"Oil services firms' revenues depend on spending from the major oil companies. It would take a sustained cutback in spending before the services companies would be hurt," Dotterer said.
